solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: English question boxer's energy level

parts.note: the boxer is Muhammad Ali, so the possessive gives ALI'S
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sports report noting an English query about a fighter's stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'level' is a verb here, not the adjective it first appears to be.
explanation.definitionFit: To level a score is to make the sides even, which is the verb's meaning in sport.

clue.text: Peter's OK

definitions.meaning: in old criminal slang a peter is a strongbox that a safecracker blows open

explanation.surface: Someone reporting that their friend Peter has come through unharmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the two definitions; Peter is not a person but thieves' slang for a strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves called a strongbox a peter, and something unharmed or secure is likewise described as sound.

clue.text: It is a girl who might use it

definitions.text: It is a girl who might use it

parts.note: 'tis is the old contraction of it is
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A riddle about a girl and some object she might use.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a girl called Sue might reach for a paper hanky.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper hanky is something any girl, Sue included, might use when she has a cold.

clue.text: Animal called and rushed about wildly

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, an example of an animal
to page someone is to call them over a speaker system

explanation.surface: A beast bellowed and then charged around out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on the rampage is to charge about violently and out of control.

clue.text: Almost consumed whole prey as fast as possible

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: consumed means ate
full means whole or complete
in falconry a pelt is the dead quarry a hawk has killed

explanation.surface: A predator that very nearly devoured its entire catch at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the final E from ATE. PELT as a hawk's prey is a falconry term found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for moving at top speed, with pelt meaning to hurry along.

clue.text: They are and can be eaten

definitions.meaning: people who are, i.e. who exist or live
offal organs from animals that are cooked and eaten

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark that some things both exist and are edible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They are' means 'they exist', so the first sense is those who live.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who live are, punningly, people who exist; and the organs are offal served at table.

clue.text: An age that dawned for Waterman?

definitions.text: An age that dawned for Waterman?

parts.words: An age that dawned for Waterman?
parts.note: the sign of the water carrier gives its name to an astrological age said to be dawning, as sung in the musical Hair

explanation.surface: Wondering about the era that began for someone called Waterman.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterman reads as a surname, but it is the water carrier of the zodiac; 'This is the dawning of the Age of ...' is the song from Hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign depicted as a water carrier also names the astrological age of the 1960s song.

clue.text: Complacently secretive about attack

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: sly means secretive or furtive
to mug is to attack and rob

explanation.surface: Someone acting with smug calm while quietly concerned about an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting complacently means behaving with self-satisfied superiority.

clue.text: One enters place to worship star

indicators.note: enters means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an altar is a place of worship in a church
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone goes into a shrine to venerate a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks like a celebrity being worshipped, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: Girlfriend curtailed confused scene

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a babel is a noisy, confused scene, after the tower in Genesis

explanation.surface: A girlfriend cut short an embarrassing muddled scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang term of endearment for a girlfriend or attractive young woman.

clue.text: With fine and regular features, son grew to assume power

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the word takes another inside it

parts.note: cultured means grown, as bacteria are cultured in a dish
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A young man grew up to take on authority and good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grew' looks like a verb of growing up, but it means cultured, as in a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: A face with sculptured features has clean, finely chiselled lines like a statue.

clue.text: Soup served in club is questionable

indicators.note: served in signals the dish is found within the following words

explanation.surface: The soup offered at a gentlemen's club is of doubtful quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich creamy soup, typically made with shellfish such as lobster.

clue.text: Pound for half of shares or equivalent in return

parts.note: quid is slang for a pound sterling
pro means for or in favour of

indicators.note: half of means only the first three of six letters are used

parts.note: quotas are allotted shares

explanation.surface: A deal: a pound paid for half of some stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the first half of QUOTAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase for something given in exchange, a fair trade of favours.

clue.text: Heavy blows in shelter can produce this kind of language

indicators.note: in means one word sits inside the other

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
gales are strong winds, playing on blows as punches

explanation.surface: Severe punches in a refuge prompting some kind of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy blows' suggests punches but means strong winds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers' jargon is a recognisable kind of language, dense and formal.

clue.text: Refugee from terrible regime

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are in a dreadful state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone who fled a cruel government.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is a person who has left their own country, often for political reasons.

clue.text: Engineers, when 100 finish, climb up again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
C is the Roman numeral for 100
end means finish

explanation.surface: Engineers climb again once a century of work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back up a slope or ladder is to mount it a second time.

clue.text: Qualifier braved playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moving about in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sports team that reached the finals and boldly took part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Qualifier' suggests sport; it is the grammatical term for a word that modifies.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar such a word modifies a verb or adjective, qualifying its meaning.

clue.text: Bishop arrives at gaps in fortifications

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
reaches means arrives at

explanation.surface: A bishop comes to holes in some castle walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Openings broken through a wall or defence by attackers.

clue.text: Maintain competitive tailless dog

indicators.note: tailless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: keen means eager or competitive
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Keep up an eager dog that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something going is to sustain it without letting it drop.

clue.text: You too, we hear, can be a drone

definitions.meaning: said aloud, these words give U-2, the American reconnaissance aircraft shot down over the USSR in 1960
an unmanned aircraft, often used for surveillance

explanation.surface: Telling someone that they, too, could be a boring talker.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense works by sound: 'you too' gives U-2, the US high-altitude aircraft brought down over Soviet territory in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveillance aircraft, and unmanned drones now do the same reconnaissance job.

clue.text: State injection must support most of weak

indicators.note: in a down entry the lower piece supports the one above it
most of means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: puny means weak
a jab is an injection

explanation.surface: An injection is needed to prop up a feeble patient's condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must support' places JAB below the trimmed PUNY in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of northern India, also a province of Pakistan.

clue.text: Such regions can be hellish or Dutch

definitions.text: Such regions can be hellish or Dutch

parts.words: Such regions can be hellish or Dutch
parts.note: the underworld is called the lower regions by this word, and the Low Countries take their name from the same word plus 'lands'

explanation.surface: A remark that certain places may be either infernal or Netherlandish.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means lower: the infernal regions below, and the Low Countries, whose name adds 'lands' to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lower or under, describing both the underworld and the low-lying Dutch lands.

clue.text: Sound of new lice rambling in kernels

indicators.note: sound of means a word spoken aloud gives the letters

parts.note: the word new said aloud sounds like nu, the Greek letter

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A noise from freshly hatched insects wandering among grains.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the central core, so kernels at the heart of atoms or cells.

clue.text: Final large policeman in charge of instrument for viewing organs

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, relating to such an instrument, which is a noun

parts.note: end means final part
OS stands for outsize, the clothing label for large
a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: A senior police officer is placed in charge of a medical scope.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'of instrument for viewing organs', an adjective, so 'of' belongs to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to an instrument passed inside the body to look at internal organs.

clue.text: Sign for Northern stream

definitions.meaning: a gesture or nod summoning someone
in Northern England a brook is called by this name

explanation.surface: A sign pointing the way to a stream in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture of summoning, and the northern English dialect word for a brook.

clue.text: Aviemore slope — maybe slow down, only kilometre to go

indicators.note: to go means the letter is removed

parts.note: to brake is to slow down, one way of reducing speed
K is the abbreviation for kilometre

explanation.surface: A driver nearing the end of a ski resort run, perhaps easing off with one kilometre left.
explanation.walkthrough: Aviemore is a Scottish Highland ski resort, hence the Scots word for a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word for a hillside or bank, fitting a Highland town.

clue.text: Heavenly body posed on vessel

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat means posed
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A beautiful figure modelled while perched on a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet, a celestial body of the solar system with rings.

clue.text: Seven Taureans I pleased excitedly

indicators.note: excitedly suggests the letters are jumbled in a rush

explanation.surface: Seven people born under Taurus delighted the speaker greatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taureans' suggests people born under Taurus; it means stars in the constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seven Sisters star cluster lies in the constellation Taurus.
